kind: A float control and a spiking test at full size, and a screen by slope on the server's test bed: pools that divide the stream by its spread (its energy) in place of its summed activity.
why: full_size_layout_in_floats.json: the stack's pool in place of every LayerNorm costs the Transformer 0.0691; full_size_centring_in_floats.json: taking the mean out first recovers only 0.0056 of that (the centred pool still costs 0.0636), so the price is the division. The pool divides by the stream's mean absolute activity; a LayerNorm (and an RMSNorm, which does not centre either) divides by the root mean square. The two agree where the channels fire alike and part where a few channels fire much more, which is where the norm must hold the loud channels down. Cortex divides by energy: in the normalization model (Heeger 1992; Carandini and Heeger 2012) a neuron's response is divided by the pooled squared activity of its neighbours. An energy pool (--pool-energy, this commit) lets every inhibitory pool of a stack's reads, cells and output hear the whole part of the square root of the stream's summed squared counts times its number of channels: the summed counts where the active channels fire alike, more where a few are loud. Whole counts in and out, the stream cut anywhere fires the same spikes, the parameters and the pools' caps unchanged.

arms.fs-tf3-spool (float control): sched/bin/full.sh transformer fs-tf3-spool --transformer-norm spool: every LayerNorm becomes the pool divided by the stream's root mean square in place of its mean absolute activity, no centring; 34,740,247 parameters, as fs-tf3-pool
arms.fs-loop6-lift-en (full size): sched/bin/full.sh stack fs-loop6-lift-en --lr 6e-4 --stack-loop 2,8,2 --pulse-budget 507000 --pool-lifts-ceiling --pool-energy: the lifted loop with energy pools; 34,810,900 parameters, as fs-loop6-lift
arms.en (test bed): sched/bin/arm.sh stack --lr 1.2e-3 --seed 2000X [--steps 6000] --pool-energy: the delayed bed with energy pools; 5,249,060 parameters, as the bed

base: Float: fs-tf3 1.305716 (LayerNorm), fs-tf3-pool 1.374858, fs-tf3-cpool 1.369304. Full size: fs-loop6-lift 1.300729. Test bed: bed24-lr12-s1 1.486381, bed24-lr12-s2 1.492556, rd-base-6k-s1 1.621562, rd-base-6k-s2 1.628309.
runs: fs-tf3-spool, fs-loop6-lift-en, en-6k-s1, en-6k-s2, en-24k-s1, en-24k-s2 on GPU 0 at priority 36 in the window of 2026-11-25, on a new code copy of the commit that records this (v18g, launch-checked on the server's CPU first): the float control and the full-size pilot first.
measure: The float control as full_size_layout_in_floats.json (windows of 496 bytes of history before 16 scored), paired with fs-tf3 and fs-tf3-pool. The stack's runs by arm.sh's and full.sh's scores (eval_stream.py on the first 2,000,000 validation bytes as 16 unbroken streams after 8,192 lead bytes, averaged weights), paired with the base of each seed and length and split by context (near 240, far 8,192); the pulses a byte.
reading: Float: dividing by the spread is the pool's price if fs-tf3-spool costs at most a quarter of the pool's 0.0691 against fs-tf3 (0.0173 or less); if it still costs three quarters (0.0518 or more), neither the mean nor the kind of division is the price, and the next diagnostic walks what else differs (the learned rest, the gain, the bias of a LayerNorm). Full size: energy pools join the next full-length run if fs-loop6-lift-en is at least 0.005 better than fs-loop6-lift with the paired interval clear of zero; between 0 and 0.005 better a second seed decides; worse, they stay off at full size whatever the bed shows. Test bed: the shared reading of experiments/read_lead_study.py (--arm energy en-24k-s1 en-24k-s2 --arm-short energy en-6k-s1 en-6k-s2 against bed24-lr12 and rd-base-6k): a fix, a constant gain or a fail; a mean lead of at least 0.005 after 24,000 updates with both seeds ahead adopts it on the bed. The stack's own readings decide for the stack; the float control says why.
seen_before_recording: full_size_layout_in_floats.json and full_size_centring_in_floats.json with their results; tests/test_pool_energy.py and the spread control's test (the whole suite passes). No run with an energy pool or a spread control has trained.

result_float.reading: The kind of division is the pool's price. The pool dividing by the stream's root mean square costs the Transformer 0.0020 against its LayerNorm, within a quarter of the pool's 0.0691 (0.0173), so 0.0672 of the 0.0691, 97%, is the division by the mean absolute activity; without centring, with the pool's rest and gain. A pool must divide by the stream's energy: what the stack's own readings below say about whole spike counts is separate.

result_bed.reading: Fail. After 24,000 updates the energy pool trails the bed by 0.0030 on the mean, one seed 0.0045 ahead and one 0.0105 behind, far from a lead of 0.005 with both seeds ahead; after 6,000 it trailed by 0.0087. Pulses a byte within half a percent of the bed's. In floats the same division is nearly free (above), so the whole counts or the spiking pool's way of dividing keep the gain from the stack on the bed. The full-size pilot fs-loop6-lift-en still decides for full size by its own reading.

result_full_size.pairing: fs-loop6-lift-en against fs-loop6-lift (1.300729): +0.0040 [+0.0032, +0.0048] over 4,160 pieces of 512 bytes (behind)
result_full_size.reading: Worse, so energy pools stay off at full size. With the membranes' ceiling lifted, so that a stronger pool takes no range from the neurons, the lifted loop with energy pools is 0.0040 behind the same loop with pools of summed activity, behind on new contexts (0.008) and far copies (0.012). The price the float control found in a Transformer (result_float) does not carry over to the stack's whole spike counts in this form.
